subject: Azure Marketplace private plan listing — SKU, SLA credits & procurement next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Byrne <sarah.byrne@brightedgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Listing & commercial terms for Azure Private Plan - BrightEdge Health

Sarah —

Great to connect — thanks for the productive initial call yesterday. Per our discussion, attaching the high-level commercial summary for the Azure Marketplace private plan we propose for BrightEdge Health. Highlights:

- Private SKU: RWI-AZ-PRIV-001 (single-tenant private plan)
- Monthly committed units and billing via Azure Merchant (billing flow to be aligned with BrightEdge PO)
- Co-sell: standard marketplace co-sell/certified partner routing; revenue split unchanged from our prior outline
- SLA / service credits: we proposed a standard SLA credit path (see attachment) — we are happy to negotiate specific caps and measurement windows with procurement/legal

Attachments: Redwood_Azure_Private_Commercials_v1.pdf (commercial summary + proposed SLA language stub)

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement sends any mandatory contract language / PO template (if you have a preferred addendum format we can redline)
2) We finalize SLA credit caps and measurement windows so Azure Seller Ops can approve the private plan listing
3) Target: submit listing to Azure marketplace review by 2027-06-14 to hit your desired onboarding window.

Are you available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the commercial bullets and clarify procurement asks?

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Re: Listing & commercial terms for Azure Private Plan - BrightEdge Health

Marcus —

Thanks for the note and the attachment. Quick procurement questions before we loop legal:

- SLA credits: we need explicit language on measurement (Azure metrics + 15-minute resolution), cure period, and the credit calculation (percent of monthly invoice for impacted SKU). Also please confirm whether credits are automatic or require a claim.
- Credit caps: our typical starting point in negotiations is single-incident cap of 20% of monthly billing and an annual aggregate cap of 60%. Is Redwood able to accept those bounds or propose an alternative?
- SOC2 + data residency: please provide your latest SOC2 Type II report and confirmation of data processing locations for the private plan.
- PO/Procurement flow: attached our PO template — we prefer the PO + signed addendum flow for marketplace billing.

Can you send redlines to the SLA addendum and confirm timeline? We need marketplace listing approved within 3-4 weeks to align with our internal launch schedule.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Regards,
Sarah Byrne
Head of Procurement
BrightEdge Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T12:25:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightEdge procurement questions — need legal + finance input

Team — forwarding Sarah's procurement email. Key asks: credit caps and SOC2 + data residency evidence. BrightEdge proposes single-incident 20% / annual 60% as a starting point and wants automatic credits when measured via Azure telemetry.

My suggested internal stance (open to pushback):
- Single-incident credit cap: 15% of monthly invoice (prorated by impacted units)
- Annual aggregate cap: 50% of annual committed spend for the SKU
- Credit claim: automated issuance when Azure Marketplace telemetry confirms SLA breach, but require customer to accept credit application in writing for any discretionary exceptions
- Measurement window: 5-minute Azure metrics feed aggregated into 15-minute windows; 30-day rolling calculation for availability metrics

Timing constraint: BrightEdge needs approval in ~3 weeks. We will need Azure Seller Ops signoff on any non-standard credit caps.

Please review and advise redline language. Attaching an internal draft SLA addendum to start from.

Thanks,
Marcus

---
Attachment: proposed-sla-addendum-draft.docx

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: BrightEdge procurement questions — need legal + finance input

Marcus / Marissa —

Thanks for the summary. I reviewed the draft and BrightEdge's proposal. Below are my recommended positions and language to include in the addendum we will send to BrightEdge:

1) Credit caps
- Single-incident credit: not to exceed 25% of the monthly invoice for the impacted SKU (we can concede to 25% rather than 20% to speed approval).
- Annual aggregate cap: capped at the equivalent of 3 months of monthly fees for the SKU (approx. 300% of monthly fee) or 100% of annual committed spend — recommend we present "annual aggregate not to exceed 100% of annual fees" (this keeps the math clear).

2) Measurement and claim process
- Measurement: availability to be calculated using Azure Marketplace telemetry (defined in addendum) aggregated in 15-minute windows.
- Automated credits: where telemetry shows an SLA breach, credits will be issued automatically on the next billing cycle unless Azure Seller Ops flags dispute. Customer may submit supporting evidence within 30 days for exceptional circumstances.

3) Remedies and exclusions
- Exclude: downtime due to scheduled maintenance (48-hour notice), force majeure, and customer misconfiguration.

4) Marketplace and seller ops approval
- Note that any deviation from the Azure Marketplace standard private plan template (including caps above standard thresholds) requires Seller Ops review and may delay listing. We should open the ticket concurrently with sending the redline.

5) SOC2 + data residency
- Confirmed: Redwood will provide a SOC2 Type II summary (redacted) and the private plan will be hosted in Azure US regions (Primary: East US; Secondary: West US) — include a short attestation paragraph. Procurement can request the full report under NDA if needed.

I'll draft the redline and circulate. Can David confirm billing/merchant implications for 25% single-incident / 100% annual cap and whether Azure merchant plumbing supports automatic credit issuance?

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com

Date: 2027-05-31T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Listing & commercial terms for Azure Private Plan - BrightEdge Health

Sarah —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the PO template. Per Soojin's redlines (attached) and our internal alignment, we've prepared a single consolidated addendum that implements the agreed measurement approach and the following credit profile:

- Single-incident credit cap: up to 25% of the monthly invoice for the impacted SKU (prorated by affected units)
- Annual aggregate cap: not to exceed 100% of the annual fees for the SKU
- Measurement: Azure Marketplace telemetry aggregated into 15-minute windows; automatic credit issuance on next billing cycle unless disputed by Seller Ops

Next steps:
1) Signing: I've uploaded the redlined addendum to DocuSign for execution: https://docusign.com/r/abc123
2) PO: Please return a signed BrightEdge PO referencing DEAL-78942 so we can route to Azure merchant billing.
3) Azure ticket: We're opening an Azure Seller Ops case today to request approval for the private plan listing with the above credit profile and will share the case number once created. That step is required for your marketplace onboarding timeline.

If the credit caps are acceptable, please sign the addendum via DocuSign and send the PO. If you need any tweaks, we can patch quickly but please note any changes may affect Seller Ops timing.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
